How to use

  • Diffuse 1–2 drops with orange through a cold winter evening.
  • Dilute to no more than 0.5% for any skin application.
  • Add a drop to a surface spray with lemon and tea tree.

Dilute before applying to skin and patch-test first. Not for internal use.

Scent profile

  • Sweet spice
  • Warm wood
  • Sharp eugenol

What's in it

  • 100% pure Syzygium aromaticum bud oil

Who it's for

Winter diffuser blends

One or two drops with orange and cinnamon is the whole of a seasonal blend.

Homemade cleaning products

Earns a place in a surface spray, where the strength is useful rather than a problem.

Experienced users

Not a beginner's oil. It demands attention to dilution in a way most of our range does not.

What people get wrong

Applying it to gums or teeth. This is widely repeated advice and it is how people end up with chemical burns and damaged tissue. Clove oil is not a dental treatment and we do not sell it as one.

Using it at normal dilutions. Half a per cent is the ceiling on skin. Most oils tolerate two or three per cent; clove is in a different category entirely because of its eugenol content.

What it won't do

It is a strong skin sensitiser, and sensitisation is permanent once it happens. If you are not confident about measuring a 0.5% dilution, this oil is not the right place to start.

Avoid it in pregnancy, keep it away from children, and do not diffuse it around pets.

We describe how our oils smell and how people use them. We don't make medical claims, because essential oils aren't medicine.

Questions about Clove Bud

Can I use it for toothache?

No, and we will not advise it. Putting clove oil on gums is common folk advice and a common cause of chemical burns to soft tissue. See a dentist.

Why is bud oil better than leaf or stem?

Bud oil is sweeter, rounder and less harsh. Leaf and stem oils are much cheaper, higher in eugenol and noticeably coarser, and they are often what you get when a bottle just says 'clove oil'.

What is the maximum safe dilution?

0.5% on skin — roughly one drop in two teaspoons of carrier. Above that the risk of sensitisation rises sharply, and sensitisation does not go away.

How long does it keep once opened?

Two to three years stored properly — cool, dark and tightly closed. Distilled oils keep considerably better than cold-pressed citrus.

What dilution should I use on skin?

Lower than most. A strong skin sensitiser. Keep to 0.5% or below on skin, avoid in pregnancy, and keep well away from children and pets. For general use, dilute into a carrier oil such as jojoba and patch-test on a small area first.

Can I take it internally?

No. None of our oils are food grade and none are sold for internal use. Essential oils are extremely concentrated, and advice to add them to water or food is not advice we endorse.

How quickly will it arrive?

Orders are dispatched from Delhi within two business days and usually arrive within a further three to five, depending on where you are. Shipping is free over ₹999.
